messages.subject: variable declaration overhead?
parts:
Hi folks,

I'm trying to balance the efficiency and human-readability of my code. I make use of the "Matt trick", examples of which typically create a matrix in the transformed variables section with as many columns as there are variables that need sampling from the multivariate gaussian, looking something like:

transformed parameters {
vector[3] beta[N];
for (n in 1:N) {
beta[n,1] <- par1 + e_beta[n,1] * tau[1]; 
beta[n,2] <- par2 + e_beta[n,2] * tau[2];
beta[n,3] <- par3 + e_beta[n,3] * tau[3];
}
}

While concise, a more readable form might be:

transformed parameters {
real par1Sample[N];
real par2SampleN];
real par3Sample[N];
for (n in 1:N) {
par1Sample[n] <- par1 + e_beta[n,1] * tau[1]; 
par2Sample[n] <- par2 + e_beta[n,2] * tau[2];
par2Sample[n] <- par3 + e_beta[n,3] * tau[3];
}
}

(i.e. permitting one to refer later to the lists of parameter samples by name rather by column index from the matrix). However, is there any cost in terms of compute efficiency incurred by the extra declarations that I should be worried about? In my real-world use, I'll be looking to sample for possibly a dozen or so parameters. 

Thanks,

Mike

--
Mike Lawrence
Graduate Student
Department of Psychology & Neuroscience
Dalhousie University

~ Certainty is (possibly) folly ~

On 6/24/13 1:25 PM, Mike Lawrence wrote:
> Hi folks,
>
> I'm trying to balance the efficiency and human-readability of my code.

I feel your pain. My advice is to start with readable code, then
gradually optimize it if you need to.

More below.

> I make use of the "Matt trick", examples of which
> typically create a matrix in the transformed variables section with as many columns as there are variables that need
> sampling from the multivariate gaussian, looking something like:
>
> transformed parameters {
> vector[3] beta[N];
> for (n in 1:N) {
> beta[n,1] <- par1 + e_beta[n,1] * tau[1];
> beta[n,2] <- par2 + e_beta[n,2] * tau[2];
> beta[n,3] <- par3 + e_beta[n,3] * tau[3];
> }
> }
>
> While concise, a more readable form might be:
>
> transformed parameters {
> real par1Sample[N];
> real par2SampleN];
> real par3Sample[N];
> for (n in 1:N) {
> par1Sample[n] <- par1 + e_beta[n,1] * tau[1];
> par2Sample[n] <- par2 + e_beta[n,2] * tau[2];
> par2Sample[n] <- par3 + e_beta[n,3] * tau[3];
> }
> }
>
> (i.e. permitting one to refer later to the lists of parameter samples by name rather by column index from the matrix).
> However, is there any cost in terms of compute efficiency incurred by the extra declarations that I should be worried
> about? In my real-world use, I'll be looking to sample for possibly a dozen or so parameters.

Your second version will be a bit faster, but not so much
as you'd notice it with a stopwatch. (The reason is
less indexing).

Depending on how you feel about matrix operations, I'd think
the clearest thing to write would be:

vector[3] tau;
...
matrix[N,3] beta;
beta <- par1 + e_beta * tau;

I'd also suggest indenting for readability if the lack of
indentation wasn't caused by too-clever mailers.

- Bob
